cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, and friend, it's short but it is LOADED. David tells us what the LORD said to someone David calls my Lord. Lean in, because this is one conversation you do NOT want to miss.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to the one David calls my Lord. What does the LORD tell Him to do?

answers.text: Go out ahead of My army

cards.question: The LORD tells David's Lord to sit at the LORD's right hand until the enemies of David's Lord come and make peace with Him.

cards.text: His enemies, made a footstool for His feet. And friend, I know footstool life, because in that junk drawer takeout menus sat on ME for YEARS.

Centuries later, Jesus asks the Pharisees, the religious leaders, whose son the Christ is, and they say David's. So Jesus points them right to this line and asks how David can call Him Lord (Matthew 22:41-45).

cards.question: Next, the LORD extends the mighty scepter of David's Lord. Where does it reach out from?

cards.text: From Zion the LORD tells Him, “Rule in the midst of Your enemies.” Then David turns to His people on His day of battle.

cards.question: On the day of battle for David's Lord, His people have to be dragged into the fight.

cards.text: WILLING, friend, and that is HUGE, because you ask the group chat who can help move a couch and suddenly everybody's phone is dead. Then David paints it in big pictures: holy splendor, the womb of the dawn, the dew of Your youth.
Now the LORD makes an oath, and He will not change His mind. Me? I change my mind about toppings forty times a batch, so that line right there is humbling.

cards.question: The LORD swears an oath to David's Lord. What does He swear this Lord will be?
The LORD swears that David's Lord will be a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek. In Genesis 14, Melchizedek meets Abram after a battle, and he's king of Salem and ___ of God Most High.

cards.text: And the book of Hebrews connects it for us: Jesus has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 6:20).
Next, David says the Lord is at Your right hand. And a day of wrath is coming.

cards.question: David says the Lord is at Your right hand. In the day of His wrath, He will crush ___.
David says that in the day of His wrath, the Lord at Your right hand will judge only inside Israel's borders.

cards.text: He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead, and crush the leaders far and wide. Then the psalm ends on a quiet picture: He drinks from the brook by the road.

cards.question: In the psalm's last line, the One who crushes kings and judges the nations drinks from the brook by the road, and therefore He lifts up His head. What picture does that leave you with?
